title: A predictive, causal theory of whole immune responses

concept.text: Proposed innovation: a quantitative explanation of how an immune response unfolds that can predict what will happen when the system is deliberately changed. Its target is the joint behavior of immune populations over time, incorporating recognition, cell states, tissue context, exposure history, signaling and feedback. It would connect these interacting features to the direction, timing and magnitude of a response, including under interventions outside the conditions used to construct the theory.

Conceptual distinction: predicting recognition is only one component of the proposed framework. The broader question is how recognition and subsequent interactions produce protection, tissue injury, persistence or resolution. A causal theory would need to make predictions about interventions that distinguish its explanation from alternatives; fitting observed patterns alone would not establish that capability. “Whole” describes the ambition to account for interacting immune processes, while any demonstrated version would still have explicit biological and practical boundaries.

significance.text: Conditional significance: a successfully validated framework could turn measurements of immune components into an explanation of their coordinated behavior and a means of predicting unfamiliar interventions. Its revolutionary contribution would be a shared explanatory framework spanning immune populations and their interactions. It could help identify which control points change a response, when they matter and how their effects depend on context.

Conditional downstream possibilities: predicting whether a particular person's response to infection, vaccination or treatment will protect them, damage tissue or fail to resolve would require additional validated links between modeled immune responses and clinical outcomes, together with sufficient information about that person. Treatment selection would be a further application requiring clinical validation. Accurate predictions of cellular changes would not by themselves establish either individual clinical prognosis or improved treatment outcomes.

Limit on impact: success within specified tissues, populations or diseases would be a major advance without establishing a universal theory of immunity. A model's usefulness could depend on which states can be measured, which interventions it covers and how far ahead it predicts. Mechanistic explanation, predictive accuracy and clinical usefulness are related achievements that would each need appropriate evidence.

missing_breakthrough.text: Proposed unsolved capability: an integrated account that reliably predicts intervention effects beyond its construction conditions. The supplied material does not establish how close existing systems are to this goal or which parts remain absent across the field. The research target should therefore be preserved without treating the lack of inspectable evidence here as proof that no relevant capability exists.

Conceptual engineering barriers: the framework would need to connect events at different biological scales and times, represent changes in cell state and tissue context, and account for exposure history and feedback. It would also need to distinguish different causal explanations that can fit the same observations but predict different intervention outcomes. These are requirements implied by the proposed scope, rather than barriers independently documented by the supplied source.

Proposed scientific requirements include informative longitudinal measurements and perturbations, ways to represent incompletely observed immune states, and explicit uncertainty about predictions. Generalization would need to survive changes in donors, tissues, diseases and interventions rather than relying on similarities to training conditions. Linking those predictions to clinical outcomes would add a separate validation problem. No numerical performance ceiling or established solution to these requirements is documented in the supplied evidence.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies Viñas Torné et al., “Systema: a framework for evaluating genetic perturbation response prediction beyond systematic variation,” gives DOI 10.1038/s41587-025-02777-8 and reports an online publication date of 25 August 2025. It describes a general cellular perturbation benchmark as finding that performance on previously unseen perturbations is harder to achieve than conventional metrics indicate. These are reported details from the research input: the validated review could not verify the article identity, date, DOI, abstract or findings because the retained PubMed artifact contained only a cookie-access notice.

Even if that reported benchmark characterization is confirmed, an evaluation of general cellular perturbation prediction would inform evaluation methods rather than establish the capabilities or limitations of theories of whole immune responses. Predicting a cellular response and predicting coordinated immune behavior across tissues, donors and disease settings involve different scopes. The supplied material provides no inspectable scientific result demonstrating the proposed whole-response capability, but this evidentiary limitation does not show that the reported benchmark result is false.

Access and currency limitations: the research says the publisher page failed to open and its account relied on a PubMed abstract, but the validated review could not verify that access history or recover the abstract from the retained artifact. The source index records a saved artifact retrieved on 11 November 2026; saving that artifact does not establish that scientific article content was captured. No bounded freshness-search record was supplied for the review's 1 November 2026 checkpoint, so the inputs do not establish a comprehensive current state of the field.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: define the tissues, donor populations, disease settings and intervention classes in advance, then prospectively predict responses to previously untested perturbations. Predictions should specify direction, timing, magnitude and uncertainty over prespecified time horizons. Where clinical relevance is claimed, define the relevant clinical endpoint and what counts as a meaningful effect before outcomes are observed. These are proposed criteria, not established standards or published consensus thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Prospectively predict untested perturbation response trajectories with stated uncertainty

completion_criteria.text: Proposed causal test: manipulate control points identified by the theory and compare the resulting response trajectories with predictions from specified competing explanations. Choose interventions for which those explanations make distinguishable predictions, so that success tests the causal account rather than merely its ability to fit familiar observations. Evaluate immune measurements and any claimed clinical consequences separately.
completion_criteria.label: Control point interventions distinguish causal predictions from competing explanations

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: repeat the prospective tests in independent cohorts and laboratories, document measurement and intervention requirements, and report failures as well as successful predictions. Evaluate uncertainty and performance when relevant information is missing or conditions differ from those used to construct the model. Finite tests would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested domain, not literal universality; broader claims would require additional evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Reproduce prospective tests independently and report failures and practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Conceptual mapping from the supplied roster: IMM-01, “A general decoder for T-cell antigen recognition,” concerns a recognition capability that could provide inputs to IMM-02. IMM-02 asks how recognition combines with cell states, tissues and interactions to produce a response. IMM-11, “Causal mechanisms that initiate the breakdown of self-tolerance,” targets a particular causal transition that a broader immune-response theory might incorporate; explaining that transition would remain a distinct achievement.

IMM-03, “Vaccine design that reliably directs broadly protective antibody evolution,” and IMM-12, “Programmable trained immunity with predictable protection and safety,” concern particular ways of directing immune behavior. They could supply intervention domains and tests for IMM-02. A general response theory would not itself demonstrate reliable antibody evolution, programmable trained immunity, broad protection or safety.

IMM-04, “Durable, antigen-specific reversal of established autoimmunity,” and IMM-05, “Routine donor-specific transplant tolerance without lifelong immunosuppression,” concern durable therapeutic outcomes. IMM-06, “General immune eradication of heterogeneous solid tumors,” and IMM-07, “Immune-mediated, treatment-free control of established HIV infection,” likewise define disease-specific outcomes. IMM-02 could help explain or predict interventions in these settings, while each outcome would require its own demonstration of efficacy, durability and applicable patient scope.

IMM-08, “Restoration of youthful immune competence in older adults,” concerns functional restoration across aging contexts. IMM-09, “In-body programming of immune cells as an inexpensive, scalable treatment,” concerns a treatment and delivery capability. IMM-10, “Real-time immune control of life-threatening systemic inflammation,” concerns timely intervention during an acute response. IMM-02 could inform restoration targets, programming choices or control policies, but would not establish rejuvenation, scalable delivery or real-time clinical control.

IMM-13, “Predictive causal control of microbiome–immune interactions,” and IMM-14, “Causal, bidirectional control of neuroimmune circuits,” focus on interfaces between immunity and other biological systems. They overlap with the contextual and feedback mechanisms that IMM-02 aims to represent, while retaining distinct requirements for causal prediction and control at those interfaces. More generally, IMM-02 sits conceptually within systems immunology and overlaps with causal inference, dynamical systems and perturbation modeling; none of these overlaps merges the roster entries.

brief.title: Predicting how an immune response will unfold
possible: Researchers could predict how the body's defenses would respond to an unfamiliar intervention: which cells would react, how strongly and for how long. The explanation would connect interacting cells, their surroundings and past exposures.
why: This would help researchers identify where and when to intervene to change an immune response. It would connect measurements of separate immune components to an explanation of how they work together.

sources.showed: They found that common scoring methods can overstate how well models predict the effects of unfamiliar genetic changes. Their Systema framework separates effects specific to a change from patterns shared across experiments.
sources.quote: Using standard evaluation metrics, we find that these simple baselines surprisingly perform comparably to the state-of-the-art methods.
sources.cited_for: Tests must distinguish predictions of a particular intervention from predictions that merely reproduce shared patterns.
sources.not_established: This evaluates changes within cells, rather than coordinated immune responses across cells and tissues.

sources.who: Robert Moore and colleagues, University of Nebraska-Lincoln
sources.showed: They built a model linking immune cells and their signals across infections, autoimmune disease and lung transplantation. It reproduced several published findings that were not used to build it.

sources.cited_for: A shared model can reproduce immune behavior across several disease settings.
sources.not_established: Agreement with published observations does not establish prospective predictions of unfamiliar interventions or individual outcomes.

sources.who: Laura D Weinstock and colleagues, Georgia Institute of Technology
sources.showed: In laboratory-grown macrophages, immune cells involved in inflammation and repair, they used a predictive model to control the duration and strength of an inflammatory marker.
sources.quote: Moreover, the identified model enabled the design of time-varying input trajectories to experimentally sustain the duration and magnitude of iNOS expression.
sources.cited_for: Models can guide interventions that produce a predicted immune-cell response over time.
sources.not_established: Control of a marker in a laboratory cell system does not establish control of interacting immune populations in tissues.

sources.showed: They inferred interactions among cytokines, the immune system's messenger molecules. Experiments supported predictions about combinations of interventions that had not been used to fit the model.
sources.quote:
We validate several model
predictions against experimental data that were not used for model fitting.
sources.cited_for: Models of interacting immune signals can predict effects of untested intervention combinations.
sources.not_established: These tests concern a limited signaling network, rather than a whole immune response.

shown: Moore and colleagues have combined many interacting immune components in a model spanning several diseases. Its predictions matched some independent published observations, although it also produced disagreements.

Weinstock and colleagues experimentally controlled an inflammatory marker over time. Jansen and colleagues tested predictions for combinations of changes to immune signals. These demonstrate useful pieces of the broader capability.
missing: An integrated explanation still needs prospective tests of unfamiliar interventions across interacting immune populations.
Tests need to distinguish competing explanations that fit existing observations but predict different intervention effects.
Independent laboratories need to reproduce prospective results and establish where predictions fail.
Predicting a person's clinical outcome or selecting treatment requires separate clinical validation.

milestones.label: Untested interventions produce the predicted response over time
milestones.explanation: Prospective tests would have to predict direction, timing and size of responses, with uncertainty, within predefined biological settings. This would test whether predictions extend beyond the conditions used to build the theory.

milestones.label: Interventions distinguish competing explanations
milestones.explanation: Changing control points identified by the theory would have to produce responses that distinguish its predictions from competing explanations. This would test whether it explains what causes the response.

milestones.label: Independent tests establish reproducibility and practical boundaries
milestones.explanation: Independent cohorts and laboratories would have to repeat prospective tests and report failures, information needs and limits. This would establish how broadly the theory works under practical conditions.

uncertain: Which tissues, populations, diseases and interventions should define the first convincing demonstration?
How far ahead must predictions remain useful, and what size of error would be acceptable?
How much can remain predictable when important immune states cannot be measured?

page.title: Causal prediction of human immune responses
page.definition: A mechanistic model—an explicit account of interacting biological processes—predicts how previously untested interventions change immune-cell populations and their signals over time. Prospective experiments test its causal claims across rapid innate responses and antigen-specific adaptive responses within a declared biological domain.

goal.need: Critical care illustrates one use: ARPA-H seeks immune models to guide interventions for patients facing the ICU burden below. Evaluation also matters: Systema, published on 25 August 2025, compared cellular perturbation prediction across 10 datasets and five cell lines and found that shared changes can inflate prediction scores. These results motivate tests that isolate intervention-specific effects.

completion.title: An integrated immune model passes prospective intervention tests and independent causal replication.
completion.criterion: A single mechanistic model prospectively predicts the effects of interventions absent from model construction on interacting innate and adaptive immune populations and their signals over time. Independent experiments reproduce those predictions and distinguish the model from prespecified competing causal explanations. The protocol fixes tissues, population, interventions, prediction horizons, sample sizes and acceptable errors before predictions are submitted. Achievement is restricted to that biological domain.
completion.set_by: Atlas provisional criterion, informed by the predictive immunology and immune digital twin roadmaps; no externally specified whole-response completion test was found.
completion.basis: Searched NIAID funding notices, ARPA-H CIRCLE requirements, and the 2022 and 2025 immune-model roadmaps for a whole-response completion test. None supplies shared accuracy, horizon, biological-coverage or replication thresholds. This provisional Atlas test combines the 2025 roadmap's prospective intervention challenges with independent experimental confirmation; its numerical acceptance limits require a separate protocol.

milestones.title: Model-designed stimulation brings IL-4-primed macrophage iNOS to its reference within 72 hours.
milestones.criterion: Use model-designed sequences of bacterial lipopolysaccharide and interferon-γ to bring iNOS, an inflammatory enzyme, to the normalized unit reference in RAW 264.7 mouse macrophages pretreated with 100 ng/mL IL-4 for 24 hours. The control horizon is 72 hours. Weinstock et al., published on 13 July 2020, reported this settling behavior with their second-generation model, N=8 per condition. Cells without IL-4 pretreatment overshot the reference. The paper specifies no numerical settling-error tolerance.
milestones.set_by: Weinstock et al., model-predictive-control experiment, Figure 6I and Methods; this is a study-specific laboratory endpoint.
milestones.threshold_quote: needed to obtain sustained constant iNOS expression over a 72 h control horizon

milestones.title: A cytokine-network model predicts withheld IL23 responses within the data's 99% confidence intervals.
milestones.criterion: Predict the IL23 response at 16 hours in stimulated human blood monocytes under four intervention combinations excluded from fitting: IL10 inhibition combined with TNF, IL1α/β or IL6 inhibition, or with added interferon-γ. Compare predictions with the experimental data's 99% confidence intervals. Jansen et al., published on 22 June 2022, reported all four predictions inside those intervals. Their fitting dataset measured six cytokines from 17 healthy donors, with incomplete donor coverage across conditions.
milestones.set_by: Jansen et al., withheld-intervention validation and Figure 14; this is an assay-specific comparison, not a field-wide accuracy standard.
milestones.threshold_quote: well within the 99% confidence intervals of the data (black lines).

milestones.title: A multicellular immune model matches at least 75% of the literature scenarios used in each validation.
milestones.criterion: Compare simulated cytokine behavior with corresponding literature-derived scenarios, using observations excluded from model construction; at least 75% must agree for a validation experiment to count as successful. Moore et al., published on 11 May 2026, reported 38 validation experiments and pathogen-specific agreement of 75–90%. Their model links 51 innate and 37 adaptive immune-cell types/subtypes through 37 secretory factors and 1,450 regulatory interactions. These are qualitative literature comparisons, not prospective intervention trials.
milestones.set_by: Moore et al., Results, Integrative model of the immune system; the authors explicitly define this model-validation threshold.
milestones.threshold_quote: the simulated cytokine behavior had to agree with the corresponding literature-derived scenario in at least 75% of cases.

milestones.title: An immune model's biomarker predictions are validated after actual control-point interventions.
milestones.criterion: Manipulate model-identified control points and compare subsequent measured biomarker levels with the model's predictions, using experimental systems of increasing clinical relevance. CIRCLE permits preclinical or clinical validation and delegates success criteria to its independent modelling and clinical evaluation platforms, AP2 and AP3. This milestone was written for critical illness. ARPA-H's announcement on 22 September 2026 identifies development and evaluation teams; it reports awards, not completed experimental validation.
milestones.set_by: ARPA-H CIRCLE programme, Control Point Validation metric, reproduced and clarified in its official FAQ.
milestones.threshold_quote: Performers will collect biomarker data following the successful modulation of control points for comparison with levels predicted by TA2 models.

not_found: No published protocol implementing the proposed Immune Turing Tests with numerical pass limits was found.
